# Loading inspector

<!-- Generated by scripts/sync-component-docs.mjs from ai/component-catalog.json and ai/component-composition.json. Do not edit; run `npm run catalog:sync`. -->

`@kerfjs/ui:recipe-loading-inspector` · Kerf UI · production recipe · Recipes

## When to use

A record inspector whose per-record values load asynchronously — every value-bearing component takes a shared placeholder flag, so the same chrome renders a faithful loading state and then the populated record.

- A detail or inspector view must render its real chrome while its per-record values are still loading, then swap to the populated record without duplicating markup.

**Not when:**

- Do not hand-build a separate empty-state layout, and do not use it for known progress — use LoadingSpinner for that.

## Imports

- Nothing to import: this is a reference composition.
- Declared side effects: lazy-recipe-css, individual-custom-element-registration.

No props: this entry has no JavaScript API.

## State and wiring

**The app owns:** loading lifecycle; which values are unknown; fetching, transport, and domain data.

No wiring helper.

## Geometry

Margin: composed · border: composed · padding: composed (layout role: reference-composition). `self` means the component already owns it — do not add wrapper padding, margin, or borders around it.

## Accessibility

- Each component marks itself aria-busy and disables its own controls while loading; the composition keeps labels and structure stable across the transition.

## Styling boundary

The component owns its own styles. Configure it through its props and variants; do not override its internals.

Everything else is internal: `kerf-ui-analyze` reports private or unknown `.kui-*` selectors (`KUI-L001`, `KUI-L010`), unknown or private tokens (`KUI-L002`, `KUI-L012`), and any application rule that restyles the component, forced dimensions included (`KUI-L019`).
